title: Argentina World Cup squad: Lionel Messi to play at sixth tournament, Gianluca Prestianni and Franco Mastantuono excluded
content:
Argentina have named Lionel Messi in their final 25-man squad for the World Cup, with Gianluca Prestianni and Franco Mastantuono among the notable omissions.

Benfica’s Prestianni, 20, and Real Madrid’s Mastantuono, 18, were both named in the 55-player provisional squad released on May 11, but both forwards have been cut from the reigning champions’ final squad. Chelsea’s Alejandro Garnacho has also been omitted from manager Lionel Scaloni’s final squad.

In April, Prestianni was handed a six-match ban by UEFA for homophobic conduct. This occurred during Benfica’s Champions League game against Real Madrid, in which Vinicius Jr. alleged that Prestianni had racially abused him. Prestianni denied that accusation at the time.

Earlier this month, FIFA extended Prestianni’s ban globally, meaning he would have missed Argentina’s first two World Cup matches against Algeria and Austria, should he have been included in the squad. Three of the six games are suspended for a two-year period, and the suspension only applied to UEFA-organised competitions. Jordan are Argentina’s third opponent in Group J.

Messi, 38, is set to play in his sixth World Cup. The Inter Miami forward exited his club’s final MLS game before the World Cup last Sunday with an apparent injury.

Inter Miami did not provide an official diagnosis after the match, but remarks from interim manager Guillermo Hoyos in his postgame press conference seemed to play down any potential severity.

Last week, following further tests, the club indicated Messi was suffering from “overload” in his left hamstring, with the timeline for his return still to be established.

Messi scored seven goals and provided three assists in seven games at the 2022 World Cup on his way to helping his nation lift the trophy — the first time he won the competition — and win his second Golden Ball – becoming the only player to win the award twice.

Goalkeepers: Emiliano Martinez (Aston Villa), Geronimo Rulli (Marseille), Juan Musso (Atletico Madrid),

Defenders: Gonzalo Montiel (River Plate), Nahuel Molina (Atletico Madrid), Lisandro Martinez (Manchester United), Nicolas Otamendi (Benfica), Leonardo Balerdi (Marseille), Cristian Romero (Tottenham Hotspur), Facundo Medina (Marseille), Nicolas Tagliafico (Lyon).

Midfielders: Leandro Paredes (Boca Juniors), Rodrigo de Paul (Inter Miami), Exequiel Palacios (Bayer Leverkusen), Enzo Fernandez (Chelsea), Alex Mac Allister (Liverpool), Giovani Lo Celso (Real Betis), Valentin Barco (Strasbourg).

Forwards: Lionel Messi (Inter Miami), Nicolas Paz (Como), Thiago Almada (Atletico Madrid), Giuliano Simeone (Atletico Madrid), Lautaro Martinez (Inter), Jose Manuel Lopez (Palmeiras), Julian Alvarez (Atletico Madrid).

Real Madrid midfielder Franco Mastantuono is considered the surprise omission, although his disappointing form in La Liga and scarce playing time likely kept him off the team.

Still just 18 years old, Mastantuono made a highly-publicized move from River Plate to Real Madrid last summer. The deal, according to River Plate, was worth a total of €63.2m.

After some decent performances alongside Messi during World Cup qualifying, Mastantuono fell out of favor. He remains a big piece of Argentina’s future. Meanwhile, Scaloni made a difficult decision in opting for veteran defender Nicolas Otamendi over Bournemouth’s Marcos Senesi.

Former Brighton signing Valentin Barco and Como’s Nico Paz, both 21 years of age, will add the much-needed younger legs to an aging squad. Aston Villa striker Emiliano Buendia also missed out despite a strong year in England.

Palmeiras striker José Manuel López, 25, with just three international caps, is a late-comer to the national team and will now play in his first World Cup.
